items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: and you have Becky Kilgore, and she’s a great singer

ctx.x: It’s great to see young guys doing what I guess, what would we call — sometimes we don’t want to put a label on everything — but what we’ll hear tonight at this festival. Do you have a name for the style?

No. It’s a whole mixture of different styles. You’ll hear Dave McKenna on piano solos, whose style, you wouldn’t call him a Dixieland piano player or a traditional piano player; © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

and you have Becky Kilgore, and she’s a great singer, and you wouldn’t call her traditional or anything like that, she takes more after the Ella Fitzgerald or Lee Wiley type of singing. And some of the bands will not be really Dixieland bands, they’ll be sort of like classic jazz bands.

items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: He has performed with Leon Redbone, Keith Ingham, and Rebecca Kilgore

ctx.x: Bobby Gordon was born in 1942 in Hartford, Connecticut, and was raised on Long Island. He benefited from a close relationship with clarinetist Joe Marsala and he honed his own clarinet skills with Muggsy Spanier, Louis Armstrong and Wild Bill Davison after moving to Chicago. In the 60s and 70s, Bobby played with the Jim Cullum Band, Warren Vache and Max Kaminsky. He has performed with Leon Redbone, Keith Ingham, and Rebecca Kilgore, and he recently released “Bobby Gordon Plays Bing” on Arbors Records. He…
Bobby was interviewed at the Allegheny Jazz Party in Chautauqua, New York on September 12, 1997 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
